1) We run a mixed workload that spikes for quarterly reporting windows. Can you explain how a tempo-based SKU (monthly base + burst consumption) would be priced versus a traditional commit bucket? 2) We resell to a set of regional partners and need a clear channel margin waterfall. Procurement needs: list price, your gross-to-net for partner pass-through, and any holdbacks for true-ups.

Can you send a simple matrix with (a) SKU definition, (b) list price, (c) partner net after pass-through, (d) examples for a 3x spike month? If possible by early next week.

Hi Maya —

Thanks — great questions. Quick answers up front, then I attach a clean pricing matrix:

- Tempo SKU model: monthly baseline (committed reserved capacity) + metered burst. Baseline is priced at a committed discount vs list; burst is charged at a metered per-token/node-hour rate with a secondary discount tier after a monthly burst threshold. This yields predictable baseline cost with amortized savings during spikes.

- Channel margin waterfall: we publish the list price (Marketplace SKU). For private offers we can set the customer-facing unit price and provide a partner pass-through percentage or fixed uplift. We typically structure: list price -> private-offer net to Redwood -> partner payout (percent of net) -> retention/true-up holdback (if any) for billing reconciliation.

Attached: a sample matrix showing three SKU bands, illustrative pricing for baseline vs burst, and partner net scenarios for a 3x spike month. See attached files: nebula_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx and channel_margin_workback.csv.

If that looks good, next step is to decide whether you want the private-offer to be a single blended SKU or itemized (baseline SKU + burst SKU). Itemized makes partner settlement simpler; blended is simpler for your billing.

I'll follow up with Ben to confirm tax/timelines and Camila on ops for marketplace listing.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
